Unbeknownst to the Sith, Jedi [[Seha Dorvald]] planted a tracking device on Caedus's cloak allowing the Jedi hidden on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] to track Caedus's every move.<ref name="Fury">''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]''</ref> Following Darth Caedus' death in [[41 ABY]] at the hand of his sister, the Confederation surrendered, ending the war.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

[[43 ABY|Two years later]], the [[Unification Summit]] was held on Coruscant to resolve post-war disputes between the three galactic governments, [[Natasi Daala]] of the Galactic Alliance, [[Turr Phennir]] of the Confederation, and [[Jagged Fel]] of the [[Imperial Remnant]]. On the sidelines, the Hapes Consortium of Hapes, led by Tenel Ka Djo, also agreed to unite with the larger galaxy during the signing of the galactic treaty. However, Natasi Daala, [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] of the Galactic Alliance, ordered Luke Skywalker to be exiled for 10 years for not stopping Darth Caedus. His sentence would be dismissed if he could find the reason as to why Caedus turned to the dark side. During his exile, several Jedi succumbed to [[Force psychosis]] which resulted in the involvement of [[Galactic Alliance Security]] and caused the Galactic Alliance to take a [[Anti-Jedi sentiment/Legends|hostile]] stance against the New Jedi Order.<ref name="Outcast">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]''</ref>

[[File:RingsofCoruscant.png|thumb|left|280px|The Rings of Coruscant, a mark left behind by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] occupation]]
Chief Daala's draconian reign abruptly ended when the Jedi launched a [[Plan Delta|preemptive strike]] in [[44 ABY]] to remove Daala from power by force. Due to her growing unpopularity with the Jedi Order, the Senate and the citizens of the Galactic Alliance, Daala's fall from grace was virtually uncontested and many were well pleased to be rid of her. In lieu of the unprecedented situation, the [[Office of the Chief of State]] was indefinitely suspended and its executive authority was invested in a constitutionally appointed replacement—the [[Triumvirate (Galactic Alliance)|Triumvirate]].<ref name="Conviction" />

The first of the triumvirs were [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Saba Sebatyne]] of the Jedi Order, Senator [[Haydnat Treen]] of the Galactic Alliance Senate, and General [[Merratt Jaxton]] of the [[Galactic Alliance Starfighter Command]]. Together, the three triumvirs quickly consolidated their rule over the Galactic Alliance from Coruscant, all the while representing the collective interests of the Jedi Order, the Senate and the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force|Armed Forces]].<ref name="Conviction" /> [[Abeloth]] eventually managed to take power by posing as a potential candidate of the leader of Coruscant, leading the Sith into Coruscant.<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref> In addition, a large portion of Coruscant was devastated by seismic activity caused by Abeloth as a means to get away from the Jedi.<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> After Abeloth's defeat, [[Wynn Dorvan]] became the next Chief of State.<ref name="MK">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref>

A [[Painting/Legends|painting]] titled ''[[Green Coruscant]]''<ref name="CGP">{{StoryCite|story=Celestia Galactica Photografica|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> was created after [[104 ABY]]<ref name="Date">"[[Celestia Galactica Photografica]]" was included in ''[[Star Wars Legends Epic Collection: Legacy Vol. 4]]'', which describes the stories it contains as taking place more than a [[Standard century/Legends|century]] after the events of {{Film|VI}}. The events of that [[Original trilogy|film]] took place in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', meaning that all [[Painting/Legends|paintings]] in "Celestia Galactica Photografica," including ''Green Coruscant'', must have been created after [[104 ABY]].</ref> and depicted a populated area of the planet filled wit floating structures and greenery.<ref name="CGP" />

===New Galactic Empire===
{{Quote|My Jedi brothers, Admiral Stazi, and members of the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances—we have all suffered great losses, but we cannot wait for the inevitable attack on Bastion! The time to attack Coruscant is now!|Emperor Roan Fel, motivating the Allies to liberate Coruscant from nearly a decade of Sith rule|<ref name="War 5">[[Legacy — War 5|''Legacy — War'' 5]]</ref>}}
[[File:SithTempleAttack-SWL19P05.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The Temple of the Sith, headquarters of Darth Krayt and the One Sith]]
In [[130 ABY]], control of Coruscant was wrested from the grip of the Galactic Alliance during the [[Battle of Caamas|final days]] of the [[Sith–Imperial War]]. With the fall of the Alliance and the Jedi retreat to Ossus, the galactic capital fell to the resurgent Empire, by then under the command of Emperor [[Roan Fel]]. [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]] was then replaced by Coruscant as the Imperial throne world, thus restoring the urban-wide planet as the heart of the Empire once more. Fel's control over Coruscant did not last for long, however, as the Empire's Sith [[One Sith|allies]] launched a [[Attack on Emperor Fel|coup d'état]], forcing Fel and his loyalist supporters into [[Empire-in-exile|exile]]. With Coruscant under Sith control, the Sith Lord [[Darth Krayt]] declared himself Emperor of a [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|new Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Legacy 8">[[Legacy (2006) 8|''Legacy'' (2006) 8]]</ref>

[[137 ABY|Seven years later]], [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok]] [[Battle on Had Abbadon|assassinated]] Darth Krayt and took control of the Galactic Empire during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]].<ref name="Legacy 48">[[Legacy (2006) 48|''Legacy'' (2006) 48]]</ref> Krayt, however, managed to [[Dark transfer|cheat]] [[Death/Legends|death]] and returned to Coruscant a [[138 ABY|year later]] to reclaim his throne. Wyyrlok was slain in the [[Temple of the Sith|Sith Temple]] and with his death, Coruscant and the Empire were once more under the rule of Krayt.<ref name="War 1">[[Legacy — War 1|''Legacy — War'' 1]]</ref>

Though the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord's]] return resulted in the Empire's rejuvenated war effort against its enemies, Krayt's revival also pushed them to the point of desperation. Thus, the Empire-in-exile, [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] and the New Jedi Order combined their strengths to launch a [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|major offensive on the Imperial capital]]. Their objective was to seize Coruscant in the hopes of destroying the Galactic Empire along with its Emperor and his Sith followers.<ref name="War 5" />

===Galactic Triumvirate===
{{Quote|The point is the investment. We're investing in the future of this government."''<br />''"We're investing in window dressing, not solid statecraft.|Empress Marasiah Fel and Admiral Gar Stazi discussing rebuilding efforts|<ref name="Legacy 2-1" />}}
[[File:Coruscant_reconstruction.png|thumb|left|280px|Coruscant under reconstruction after the Sith defeat]]
Following eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] rule by the [[One Sith]], the combined military might of the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]], the [[Empire-in-exile]], and the [[New Jedi Order]] defeated the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Krayt]] and his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]]. The Galactic Triumvirate was set up after the [[Second Imperial Civil War|war]] to merge the various factions into one, cohesive government. With Coruscant's liberation and the final death of Darth Krayt, the One Sith quickly lost their hold over the galaxy as the Empire collapsed into ruin without the leadership of its Emperor. The surviving members of the One Sith fled into hiding while the victorious allies united as one to form the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]], headed by Master [[K'Kruhk]] of the New Jedi Order, Admiral [[Gar Stazi]] of the Alliance, and [[Empress/Legends|Empress]] [[Marasiah Fel]] of the Empire.<ref name="War 6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref>

The new government immediately set about restoring stability to the galaxy. Reconstruction efforts began on the planet Coruscant which had suffered damage during the [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|battle]] to seize it from the Sith. The [[Imperial Mission]], abused by Darth Krayt, was disbanded. However, efforts to improve the galaxy's infrastructure were continued beginning with a [[Communications array/Legends|communications array]] that would link the Outer Rim sectors with the Core Worlds. Though not an especially costly project, it did cause political tensions.<ref name="Legacy 2-1" />

==Inhabitants==
===Citizens===
{{Main|Coruscanti/Legends}}
Coruscant was home to a variety of species, though Humans made up the majority. Most of the planet's native species were either extinct or lived in the lowest parts of the Underworld by the time of the Old Republic. The planet was thought to be the home of Humans. Though not all well known citizens were always born on Coruscant, many considered the planet their home.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Government and politics===
{{Quote|The planet thrives on the changing tide of politics, providing a stable anchor through damaging rebellions, the long-overdue fall of the corrupt Old Republic, and the sweeping introduction of the Emperor's resplendent New Order.|Pollux Hax|<ref name="TISWU" />}}
[[File:Senatebldg.png|thumb|right|250px|The Senate Building]]
Political life and government on Coruscant centered around the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] and its successor governments.<ref name="CatCW" /> During the reigns of the Old Republic and the Galactic Alliance, Coruscant was represented in the Senate. As the center of galactic government, Coruscant thrived on politics and the business of government. However, this also opened up huge opportunities for greed and corruption.<ref name="CoD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> The Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic did exercise some control over Coruscant's administration though he did not interfere with the day-to-day affairs of government.<ref name="CoD" /> This practice continued well throughout the era of the Galactic Empire with the Emperor, but Moffs [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|were placed in command]] over the [[Mayor/Legends|mayor]] of Imperial City in the form of the [[Coruscant sector/Legends|Imperial Sector]].<ref name="Empire 1">[[Empire 1|''Empire'' 1]]</ref> During the New Republic and the Galactic Alliance, the Chief of State exercised overall control of Coruscant but stayed out of day-to-day affairs.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

Until [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]], Galactic/Imperial City, had a mayor<ref name="CatCW" /> who led the [[City Municipal Authority]].<ref name="CL" /> Several of the planet's sectors also had their own local mayors and governments. The Yuuzhan Vong took direct control over Coruscant establishing a theocratic dictatorship without a local government. This lasted until the Galactic Alliance retook the planet from the Vong in 29 ABY.<ref name="DW">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref> The Galactic Alliance then established the [[Galactic City Authority]], which managed Coruscant's government and the planet's day to day affairs.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

===Law enforcement===
{{Quote|We're the law on Coruscant. Not the Jedi.|CSF Detective [[Gwad Raatu]]|<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref>}}
{{Main|Coruscant Security Force/Legends}}
{{SeeAlso|Coruscant Guard/Legends|Galactic Alliance Guard|Senate Guard/Legends}}
One of the oldest planetary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police forces]] in the galaxy,<ref name="CS">{{TORcite|type=codex|Coruscant Security}}</ref> the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] (CSF) served as the primary law enforcement during most of Coruscant's history, especially during the Galactic Republic, the New Republic, and the Galactic Alliance. It worked closely with the [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guard]] and the [[Jedi Peacekeeper]]s during the Old Republic, but maintained ultimate control of policing the planet.<ref name="GaW" /> This included regular patrols of the various districts and neighborhoods of Galactic City, criminal investigations, [[Terrorist/Legends|counter-terror]], [[Spy/Legends|counter-espionage]] operations,<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> crowd control at major events, and [[Riot|public disturbances]],<ref name="Bloodlines" /> maintaining the planet's skylanes, handing out speeding tickets,<ref name="CSWE" /> [[Bodyguard/Legends|diplomatic protection]],<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref><ref name="Backlash">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]''</ref> and responding to a variety of other emergencies and situations.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

[[File:RealStoriesOfTheCoruscantHighwayPatrol-TCaJ.png|thumb|left|250px|Coruscant Police officers]]
During the later years of the Republic, foot patrol on the upper levels was mainly the responsibility of [[GU-series Guardian police droid/Legends|police droids]], though humanoid and organic [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] were also present especially in the [[Coruscant Underworld Police|underworld police]]<ref name="SWE">{{SWE|groups|coruscant-underworld-police|Coruscant underworld police}}</ref> [[detective division]],<ref name="Senate Murders" /> and special units.<ref name="TZ" /> Special units existed for various tasks including [[Special Weapons Team|SWAT]] teams, [[Forensics Unit]], the [[Organized Crime Unit]], the [[Anti-Terrorism Unit]],<ref name="TZ" /> the [[Tactical and Operational]] force,<ref name="Bloodlines" /> the [[Customs Enforcement Division]],<ref name="Coruscant">{{TORcite|Coruscant}}</ref> and the CSF's [[Traffic Division]] which was charged with maintaining order in the massive skylanes of Galactic City.<ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="Bloodlines" />

During the Galactic Empire, the [[Coruscant Guard/Legends|Coruscant Guard]] was placed in overall command of Coruscant's security, but the CSF continued as a police force though subservient to the Guard.<ref name="Empire 1" /> After the formation of the New Republic, the Guard was disbanded and the CSF were returned to their primary status which continued throughout the Galactic Alliance. When the threat of a new civil war between Corellia and the Galactic Alliance threatened the safety of Coruscant, several CSF officers joined the new [[Galactic Alliance Guard]].<ref name="Bloodlines" /> However as the war continued and the GAG's methods became more and more brutal, most CSF officers left and returned to the CSF.<ref name="GaW" />

===Public health and safety===
{{Main|Coruscant Rescue Ops|Coruscant Health Administration}}
Fire fighting, rescue, and cleanup was performed by the [[Coruscant Rescue Ops/Legends|Coruscant Rescue Ops]]. Each planetary district maintained their own teams. Many Rescue Ops were poorly educated and underpaid, as their work was thought more fitting for droids. At the higher end of the Rescue Ops were Coruscant's fire-fighting teams; they piloted [[Emergency firespeeder/Legends|firespeeders]], wore fire and radiation-proof body suits (including bronze helmets), and were equipped with fire-suppression backpacks that fed handheld hose-guns. These teams protected the endless urban sprawl from disastrous fires and explosions.<ref name="DB CFF">{{DB|organization|coruscantfirefighter|Coruscant fire fighter}}</ref> Their duties were later continued by [[Coruscant Fire and Rescue]] during the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="Bloodlines" />

The [[Coruscant Health Office/Legends|Coruscant Health Administration]] was charged with protecting the populace from various diseases and infections that could develop and spread in a large city. They also focused on issues of drugs such as [[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]] and inoculations for new immigrants and migrants. They worked together with [[Medcenter/Legends|medcenters]] to ensure the general health of the population. However, the lower levels were mostly left to their own devices. Few had access to proper health care, police, or fire services. Most of these services were concentrated on the upper levels.<ref name="HNN49deathsticks">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_1.html|SPECIAL REPORT: The Death Stick Scourge}}</ref><ref name="HNN51virus">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|51|news/13411_3.html|Port Crowding Increases Virus Risks}}</ref>

===Entertainment and sports===
{{Main|Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Monument Plaza/Legends|Galactic Museum|Galaxies Opera House/Legends}}
[[File:Vos_Gesal_Street.jpg|thumb|right|225px|The Uscru Entertainment District]]
Coruscant had many attractions to offer its visitors and inhabitants. Chief among them was the [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]].<ref name="ItWoSWAotC">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> In it could be found the [[Galaxies Opera House/Legends|Galaxies Opera House]], a favorite location of then-Chancellor Palpatine. Coruscant was also home to the [[Coruscant Opera/Legends|Coruscant Opera]], [[Monument Plaza/Legends|Monument Plaza]], and the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]], all of which were popular tourist sites providing timeless entertainment and enjoyment.<ref name="CSWE" />

[[Chin-bret/Legends|Chin-Bret]] was one of the most popular sports on Coruscant during the last years of the Galactic Republic. The sport was played by chin-bretiers who carried [[pikers]] to play the game. The sport was most famously played at the [[T'Chuk Sporting Arena|T'Chuk Arena]].<ref name="TCD">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]], Coruscant hosted the [[Galactic Games/Legends|Galactic Games]]. During the event, an assassination attempt was made on Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="CotE" />

==Fauna==
[[File:Veermok-wosfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An escaped Veermok on Coruscant, looking for prey]]
Fugitive animals were a large component of the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-planet]] Coruscant's "wild" fauna. Many exotic trophy species were [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggled]] in from other planets for the pleasure of Coruscanti citizens. Often, these creatures remained too wild or dangerous to be domesticated, and were either surreptitiously released into Coruscant's artificial environment or escaped on their own from [[animal trade]]rs. One such species were the [[Narglatch/Legends|narglatch]], a species that made cute pets when young, though they invariably caused problems once they began to grow to maturity.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> Some of the more dangerous predatory animals even killed and ate their masters before escaping.

Though they were far from their homeworlds, many of these escaped species were able to eke out an existence on Coruscant. Some animals migrated to certain areas, like the [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] who adapted to Coruscant's cooler polar regions.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> The lower levels of Coruscant were infested by dangerous creatures like [[Anooba/Legends|anoobas]], [[saw-toothed grank]]s, and [[Veermok/Legends|veermoks]], who feasted on garbage or on other creatures. Sometimes, these creatures made it too dangerous for the inhabitants of the lower levels to go out at night.<ref name="The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

Additionally, a limited number of Coruscant's native species survived well into the planet's urbanization into an [[ecumenopolis]]. Most notably, the [[Hawk-bat/Legends|hawk-bat]] was a bird-like species that survived by preying on [[Granite slug/Legends|granite slugs]], which were a species of slug that adapted to live on the vertical surfaces of buildings. The only other species known to survive was the [[thrantcill]].

==Locations==
===Senate District===
{{Main|Federal District}}
[[File:SenateDistrict-POP.png|thumb|right|250px|The Senate District]]
The Senate District served as the ''de facto'' government capital for Coruscant. It included locations such as the Senate Building, the Republic Executive Building, the [[Galactic Justice Center]], [[500 Republica/Legends|''500 Republica'']], and the Galactic Museum. Throughout the planet's history, the Senate District was the site of numerous battles in several wars including the Great Galactic War, the Clone Wars, the Galactic Civil War, and the Yuuzhan Vong War. During the latter, the District became the center of the Vong Empire with the Senate Building serving as the house for the [[Well of the World Brain]], which controlled the Vongforming of the planet. After the war, the District once again became the center of political activity and returned to its former glory under the Old Republic.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Imperial Palace===
{{Main|Imperial Palace/Legends}}
The Imperial Palace was originally the Palace of the Republic. During the Galactic Empire's reign, it became Emperor Palpatine's official residence and was drastically expanded, becoming the largest building on Coruscant. When the New Republic captured the planet, it was converted into the main government center and the residence for the Chief of State. However, it was destroyed in the Yuuzhan Vong attack, partially when Chief of State Borsk Fey'lya detonated a bomb in his office.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Jedi Temple===
{{Main|Jedi Temple/Legends}}
[[File:JediTemple-Deceived.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Jedi Temple]]
The Jedi Temple was the seat of the Jedi Order for thousands of years. Throughout its history it was damaged several times. During the Galactic Empire it was left standing, though a damaged and burned shell of its former glory. Luke Skywalker, upon re-establishing the New Jedi Order, built the [[Jedi Headquarters]] on top of the roof of the Temple. However, it and the Temple were razed to the ground during the Yuuzhan Vong attack. The Galactic Alliance rebuilt it as the [[New Jedi Temple]], an exact replica of the old Temple, though with an added glass pyramid structure above. It remained this way until the One Sith turned it into the Sith Temple.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Coruscant's Underworld===
{{Main|Coruscant Underworld/Legends}}
The Coruscant Underworld was the area below the glittering skyscrapers of Galactic City. It was filled with crime and despair, but also with the entertainment of various kinds. It was in effect, a world of its own, with many areas controlled by gangs.<ref name="CSWE" />

===Manarai Mountains===
{{Main|Manarai Mountains}}
One of the few pieces of Coruscant's landmass that were left untouched was the Manarai Mountains, twin peaks that stuck up out of the ground near the famous Imperial Palace. The Manarai Mountains included the tallest peak, Umate. The peak contained many floating restaurants as well as Monument Plaza, and was home to the [[Flames of Umate]] cult. It was beneath the Manarai Mountains that the ''Lusankya'' was hidden. The mountains were destroyed during the Yuuzhan Vong assault on Coruscant.<ref name="CatCW" />

===Planetary defense systems===
[[File:GolanIIDefensePlatform-GA.jpg|thumb|A [[Golan II Space Defense SpaceGun|Golan II station]] in orbit over Coruscant]]
As of the Battle of Coruscant during the Yuuzhan Vong War, Coruscant had a four tier defense system. The first and uppermost tier was a series of mines. These were deactivated during the battle at the behest of [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], because he believed that they would do more harm than good, only to be reactivated by Calrissian later when the attacking Vong fleet was in the midst of the minefield.<ref name="SbS" />

The second tier was a series of [[Golan space defense platform|Golan Defense Platform]]s, mostly Golan II types. The command platform was dubbed "Orbital Defense One" and was larger than its cousins. Most of these were destroyed when the Vong broke through New Republic lines, including Orbital Defense One.<ref name="SbS" />

The third tier was a massive planetary shield, controlled by a series of hundreds of relays on the surface of Coruscant. The shield seems to have worked by some kind of dispersion of energy released onto the shield. The Vong employed a tactic that involved waves of kamikaze ships crashing into the shield, overloading the relays, and effectively bringing it down.<ref name="SbS" />

The fourth and last tier was an array of rooftop [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]], akin to the point-defense systems on some capital ships. Some were operated automatically, others by Human gunners and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]]. Also counted was the [[Proton bomb/Legends|proton bomb]] in the Chief of State's office, which was detonated when Vong soldiers occupied the Imperial Palace. The explosion destroyed the building housing the office, and the data towers on Coruscant.<ref name="SbS" />

==Economic and political rivalries==
Coruscant was not unique as a galactic hub in the galaxy after hyperdrive became common usage. 53 years after the formation of the Republic, the term "Whoever controls Coruscant controls the galaxy" was coined. During the [[Old Republic era]] and beyond, there were several urbanized planets and moons that rivaled Coruscant economically, and some that were other major governmental centers.<ref name="CSWE" />
*[[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]]: From [[17,000 BBY]] to [[3017 BBY]], the Core World Alsakan attempted to usurp Coruscant's pre-eminence as the Galactic capital seventeen times in the [[Alsakan Conflicts/Legends|Alsakan Conflicts]]. Initially driven by differences over colonization policy, with Coruscant favoring a centralized, bureaucratic state and Alsakan preferring greater local independence and initiative, the Alsakan Conflicts were fought over 14,000 years. The differences between the two planets survived the [[Pius Dea Era]], the [[Old Sith Wars]], and the [[Great Galactic War]], before the [[Seventeenth Alsakan Conflict]] was finally, decisively ended by the [[Corellian Hegemony]]. Despite the conflicts ending [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] continued to rival Coruscant economically, and culturally for the rest of known galactic history, using [[High Galactic (language)|high galactic]] as a cultural alternative to basic script.<ref name="TEGtW" /><ref name="TEA" />
*[[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]: In [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], having abandoned their homeworld of [[Varl/Legends|Varl]], took control of the moon, which was located on popular trade routes, particularly the [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|Ootmian Pabol]], and Nar Shaddaa became completely urbanized. Eventually, trade routes shifted, and the moon lost its economic opportunities. Nar Shaddaa became a haven for smugglers and criminals.<ref name="CSWE" /> Nicknamed "Little Coruscant" as the moon was heavily populated with layer on layers, it had little of the grace of Coruscant's skyline.<ref name="Annihilation">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref>
*[[Empress Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]]: In 5,000 BBY, the planet, then known as Koros Major, rose to the forefront of galactic events as the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Old Sith Empire]] attacked it. The Jedi repelled the invaders, and since then it was considered the capital of the Deep Core, even being called the "Coruscant of the Deep Core." A bastion of civilization in the impenetrable and treacherous Deep Core, it remained a major center of commerce during the times of the Empire, New Republic and Galactic Alliance. It was also intended as the original redoubt for the New Republic government to flee to during the Yuuzhan Vong War, but eventually, [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]] became favored over the ancient planet.<ref name="CSWE" />
*[[Taris/Legends|Taris]]: The planet was situated on the Perlemian Trade Route and became a major economic center in ages past. However, several new, shorter trade routes were discovered, rendering Taris obsolete. Without the support of the Republic, the planet fell into ruin and disrepair. Taris's surface was devastated by [[Darth Malak]] in [[3956 BBY]], during the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="CSWE" />
*[[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]]: Located on the Hydian Way, this prosperous and highly polluted world served as the capital of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] in the waning days of the Old Republic, the time of the Empire, and during the rise of the New Republic. However, it lost its glory after the Yuuzhan Vong War.<ref name="CSWE" />
*Denon: Throughout the waning days of the Galactic Republic, the Galactic Empire and the New Republic, Denon continued to thrive in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]. After the end of the Yuuzhan Vong War, while the Galactic Alliance and the Yuuzhan Vong were rebuilding Coruscant, Denon was chosen to serve as the temporary capital of the Alliance in 29 ABY. By 30 ABY, the galactic capital had returned to Coruscant.<ref name="CSWE" />
*[[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]]: This economic powerhouse had backed the galactic currencies since the inception of the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Galactic Credit Standard]] and remained at the center of the galactic economy. Although not rivaling Coruscant politically, its economic power remained as strong as ever, if not stronger as shown after the [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]], which led the galaxy to the brink of financial ruin. After this, it became the financial center of the Empire and remained in this position for at least the duration of the New Order. After the Yuuzhan Vong war, Muunilinst, along with Mygeeto, no longer had a tie in with Coruscant, and by 40 ABY, the Imperial Remnant had control of its credit harvest.<ref name="CSWE" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:CoruscantGlobeE1.png|thumb|left|200px|View of Coruscant from Episode I]]
The concept of a planet-wide city was developed by George Lucas as the Imperial capital in the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Revenge of the Jedi|Rough Draft]] and Revised Rough Draft of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|Star Wars Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi.'']]<ref name="Making of">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref><ref name="WCC">{{SWArchive|url=community/askjc/steve/askjc20030611.html|text=Ask the Lucasfilm Jedi Council: Who created Coruscant}}</ref> In the [[The Star Wars rough draft|Rough Draft]] of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the Imperial capital was named [[Alderaan (The Star Wars)|Alderaan]], but [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] ultimately became the name of [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]'s homeworld.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> During the development of ''Return of the Jedi'', the planet was called [[Had Abbadon]].<ref name="TSWA">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes IV–VI, 1977–1983]]''</ref> However, it was realized that such a city on screen would be impossible given the technical limitations at the time, thus the planet did not appear in the fim.

The capital was introduced in Star Wars media by the [[1991]] [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] novel, ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' by [[Timothy Zahn]], who chose to name it "Coruscant".<ref name="TZI">{{Reddit|url=r/StarWarsEU/comments/qrlyjm/author_timothy_zahn_on_his_naming_of_coruscant_in|thread=Star Wars Action News Podcast 2007 Timothy Zahn interview|archivedate=20250320080806}}</ref> Prior to that, the "Imperial Capitol" or "Empire Capitol" was first mentioned in fiction in [[Marvel Comics]]' [[Star Wars (1977) 61|''Star Wars'' (1977) 61]] in [[1982]] and then briefly appeared in images of archival video seen in [[Star Wars (1977) 63|''Star Wars'' (1977) 63]].

Coruscant was first seen on screen in the [[List of changes in Star Wars re-releases|1997 Special Edition]] release of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], and later appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]]. After considering different names for the planet, Lucas decided or talked into to use "Coruscant".<ref name="WCC" /><ref name="TZI" /> The name "Coruscant" is therefore one of the few [[List of Legends elements in the films|Expanded Universe elements that made its way in to the films]]. As Zahn recalled the decision during [[Celebration III]]:

''"Just to make it clear, I did not invent the planet…George Lucas had invented the planetwide city a long time ago. When I was starting the Thrawn Trilogy, they told me to coordinate with the West End Games source material, and they had it listed as the Imperial Planet. Well nobody names a planet 'Imperial Planet,' so I thought it needed a name, so I picked the word that means glittering: 'Coruscant.' Apparently, when it came time to choose a name [for the films], people persuaded George to go with Coruscant and be done with it. So I felt very vindicated -- the tail wagging the dog. It was an honor to be slipped into the movies this way."''

The word "coruscant" is traditionally pronounced in English with a hard "c" and with the stress on the second syllable – /kəˈɹʌskənt/ (ko'-rus-kant'), and this was indeed the pronunciation usually used in early audiobooks and audio plays, such as the audio adaptations of [[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] and [[Dark Empire (audio drama)|''Dark Empire'']] or [[Chuck Benson]]'s reading of [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''The Thrawn Trilogy'']]. However, since the release of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], the word is usually pronounced /'kɔɹəsɑnt/ (ko'-ru-sant) in the ''Star Wars'' universe, with stress on the first syllable and the second "c" silent.

[[File:Planet23-Coruscant-SWR.png|thumb|225px|Coruscant as depicted in [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] (1998)]]
In various novels, characters aligned with the Empire refer to Coruscant as Imperial Center. Within the stories, this is explained as an administrative renaming undertaken to emphasize the differences between the Galactic Republic and its successor state, the Empire.

The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Coruscant in the Sesswenna sector, itself a misspelling of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] of the Core. The Seswenna sector is actually located in the Outer Rim.

===Inconsistencies===
In the large volume of material relating to Coruscant, there are conflicting statements about the ecumenopolis; inconsistencies are found mainly in sources released before 1999 when Coruscant was visually established in ''The Phantom Menace''.

Most sources, including all illustrations, show Coruscant as having negligible surface water, save for the ice caps. However, the [[The Black Fleet Crisis|''Black Fleet Crisis'' trilogy]] states that Coruscant has two continents, a large one that contains Imperial City and a smaller one. More than half of this version of the Coruscant is an ocean. No other source follows this version, though ''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]'' does refer to distinct continents, and the discrepancy is usually solved by referring to the alleged ocean as the artificial Western Sea.

[[File:TIEFighterCoruscant.png|thumb|left|225px|A different version of Coruscant, as seen in the [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] Collector's CD-ROM]]
The intro of the [[1994]] game [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] shows an orbital view of Coruscant that looks very similar to how the planet would appear in the prequel movies five years later. However, the Collector's edition, which features a remade intro, shows an Earth-like Coruscant, blue with clouds.

Another depiction of Coruscant, shown in the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|''Shadows of the Empire'' comic]], shows Coruscant as a terrestrial planet as opposed to an ecumenopolis, including green continents and a very large body of water.

===Population===
One of the most notable inconsistencies concerns the planet's population. Most recent Expanded Universe sources, such as the novel ''[[The New Jedi Order: Traitor]]'' and the sourcebooks ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'' and ''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]'', have stated a population of one trillion for Coruscant. At the last planetary census around 19 BBY, the population was around one trillion, counting only full-time registered citizens. Including the omitted, such as temporary workers and transients, the real population is said to have been triple the original count.<ref name="CNI:JT" />
